# Fix the dock lock idioms in place, before anything moves

> **AMENDED 2026-09-04.** This was "extract the lock concern into a plugin, as the vehicle spike". PR #18240 delivered that and @neo-opus-grace Dropped+Superseded it — [successor map](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/18240) — because the moved body violated four Neo idioms, none of them introduced or resolved by moving it. Her successor ordering is now this ticket's scope: **fix the idioms in place on `Workspace` first; where the code lives is the second question.**

Sub of #18151.

## Context

`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` is 4,317 lines at `origin/dev@274b63beac`, and D#18150 is choosing a vehicle to decompose it. The spike that tried extraction first produced the finding that made extraction the wrong first step: **relocating code does not improve it**, and the lock concern's body was carrying four idiom violations that travel with it wherever it goes.

Operator rating on the extraction PR: 5/5/5/5. A refactor review that checks line count, test greenness and assertion-edit count verifies only that the move was *faithful* — none of the three can see whether the moved thing was worth keeping.

## The Problem

Four idioms, all live on `dev`, none of them a consequence of any refactor:

| # | Idiom violation | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Positional pairing.** `syncDockLockAction` paired `dockItemIds`, `getTabButtons()` and `getCardContainer().items` by index, while `tab/plugin/Overflow` removes overflowing buttons from that set **by design** — so under overflow a lock transition could stamp the drag token on the wrong button. | **DONE** — PR #18245, identity-keyed via `dockItemId` |
| 2 | **Hand-rolled change detection.** Five action syncs wrote `action.x !== v && (action.x = v)` in front of reactive configs that already self-diff. | **DONE** — PR #18245, with the `setSilent`-vs-`set` batching correction from @neo-opus-grace's review |
| 3 | **Per-instance mutable state as class fields.** `dockLockPaneState` and `dockLockDragState` are `WeakMap`s keyed on components — a parallel store the engine cannot observe or invalidate, where the idiom is configs. | **open — this ticket** |
| 4 | **The engine patches a tab button's presentation imperatively.** `setSilent` / `vdom['aria-label']` / `update()` against a header that should own its own chrome, per the standing operator ruling. | **open — #18241**, which is the generator: actions have no class, so the derivation is written once in the projection and again in every host sync |

## The Architectural Reality

Item 3 is the residue after #18245 and #18241. The two `WeakMap`s exist because unlock must reverse along the path that locked: the record decides, never the current probe. That contract is right; the storage is not. A `WeakMap` keyed on a component instance is invisible to the engine's own lifecycle — nothing invalidates it on destroy except the code that wrote it, and nothing can inspect it.

Item 4 is not this ticket's to fix, and it subsumes part of item 3: once an action owns its state→presentation derivation, the drag-token record has an owner too.

## The Fix

Move the lock records off class fields and onto the surfaces that already have lifecycle: the pane's and button's own config state, or the committed document, so the engine can see and invalidate them. **Sequenced behind #18241** — the shape of item 3's fix depends on whether an action class exists to hold it.

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 — `dockLockPaneState` and `dockLockDragState` are gone from `Workspace`'s class fields; the exact-restore contract is preserved and still witnessed by the existing arms, unedited.
- [ ] AC-2 — The replacement is observable to the engine: a destroyed pane or button leaves no record behind without the lock code running.
- [ ] AC-3 — `Workspace.mjs` loses lines and gains none. The number is stated in the PR body.
- [ ] AC-4 — No extraction. If the residue looks worth moving afterwards, that is D#18150's question and a separate PR.

## Out of Scope

- **Extraction of any kind.** That was this ticket's original scope and it was the wrong first step; #18240 is the receipt.
- The action class (#18241) and the §1e trigger widening (#18242).
- D#18150's vehicle choice. This ticket makes the code worth extracting; it does not decide where it goes.

## Avoided Traps

- **Extracting first.** Measured: the extraction moved 240 lines and improved none of them, and its four ACs graded the move — so none could fail on any real falsifier.
- **Reading green arms as approval of a refactor.** 896 passing arms and a −175 delta told me nothing about whether the moved code was worth keeping.
- **Treating a reviewer's Drop+Supersede as "discard everything".** The salvage map scoped the discard to the extraction; five in-place fixes were never in it, and I binned them anyway until @tobiu caught it. They are now #18245.

## Related

- PR #18240 (closed, Drop+Supersede) — the extraction and its falsifiers; the successor map.
- PR #18245 (approved) — items 1 and 2, in place.
- #18241 — item 4's generator: actions have no class.
- #18242 — widening the `defect-note` trigger from *broke* to *touched-and-saw*, which is how items 1–4 should have surfaced years earlier.
- D#18150 — the decomposition this feeds; the declinability datum from the spike belongs in the Guard cells of options B and E.
- #18151 — parent.

## Salvaged from the spike, carried so it is not rediscovered

**A lazy-getter plugin makes declinability a call-site discipline rather than a property of the vehicle** — a declined concern still constructed through `syncDockLockItemPresentation`, because only two of four entry points gated on the flag. That belongs in D#18150's `Guard` cells for both B and E regardless of which wins. And **an extraction of the largest self-contained concern yielded ~175 lines**, which is a real input to that Discussion's target.
